name: Great Tower (the Keep)
desc: 28 m stone keep, last refuge of the castle; four storeys.

name: Inner Ward & Great Hall
desc: Lord's hall, chapel and kitchens behind a second wall.

name: Great Gatehouse
desc: Twin drum towers, portcullis and murder holes.

name: Drawbridge & Barbican
desc: Lifting bridge over the moat, guarded by a walled barbican.

name: Castle Moat
desc: Spring-fed moat ringing the castle plateau.

name: Postern Gate
desc: Small north door to the ridge paths and watch posts.

name: Market Square
desc: Heart of the town: market hall, cross, well and stalls.

name: St. Michael's Church
desc: Parish church with a 36 m spire, the tallest thing in the vale.

name: Guildhall
desc: Where the merchant guild meets and the town court sits.

name: The Ford & Crown
desc: The town's great inn - travellers, gossip and quests.

name: Steward's Hall - YOUR HOUSE
desc: Home of The Steward. Start your journey here.

name: Town gates (N, W, E & River Gate)
desc: Four gatehouses close at curfew.

name: St. Hilda's Abbey
desc: Benedictine abbey: church, cloister, infirmary and pilgrims' house.

name: Abbey fishponds
desc: Three stew ponds that feed the monks on fast days.

name: Westbrook green & chapel
desc: Village green, pond, maypole and chapel.

name: Eastmere & Eastmere Water
desc: Fishing village on a reed-fringed mere.

name: Southfold
desc: Shepherds' hamlet with a great stone sheep pen.

name: Raven Hill Watchtower
desc: Lookout with a signal beacon, in sight of the castle keep.

name: Beacon Hill Watchtower
desc: Lookout with a signal beacon, in sight of the castle keep.

name: West Tor Watchtower
desc: Lookout with a signal beacon, in sight of the castle keep.

name: Greycrown Beacon
desc: Highest point of the vale: the great warning fire.

name: The Nine Maidens
desc: Ancient ring of nine stones older than the castle. Locals leave offerings.

name: The Old Ash Ford
desc: Shallow crossing where the first settlers forded the Ash - the vale's namesake.

name: Ashford Watermill
desc: Grinds the vale's grain; the miller takes one sack in sixteen.

name: Tannery
desc: Smelly work kept downstream and outside the walls.

name: Post Windmill
desc: Turns to face the wind on a single great post.

name: Tiltyard
desc: Jousting lists for the summer tourney.

name: Quarry
desc: Where the castle's stone was cut. Still worked today.

name: King's Chase Lodge
desc: Royal hunting lodge deep in the deer forest.

name: Charcoal Burners' Camp
desc: Smoke rises day and night from the Wildwood clearing.

name: Ash Bridge
desc: Three-arched stone bridge below the River Gate.

name: East Bridge
desc: Timber bridge carrying the King's Road east.
